source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.6 Work, Energy and Power — table-of-contents scope only ('potential energy of an object at a height' confirmed under Work, Energy and Power), teaching authored from first principles. The atomic concept: near the Earth's surface a body's gravitational potential energy is U = mgh, measured from a height you CHOOSE to call zero — the choice moves every U value but never the difference ΔU = mgΔh, and that difference depends only on the start and end heights, not on the path between them. Does NOT teach the general definition of potential energy or ΔU = −W_conservative (that is potential_energy_definition, consumed as a shipped prerequisite and cited by concept_id only, never by its state numbers), does NOT teach the spring form of potential energy, does NOT convert U to K or track a moving total, does NOT treat friction losses, and does NOT touch the general −GMm/r form (a later chapter; the h << R_Earth caveat is one advanced-ring narration clause, never a formula). Built on the newtons_laws_body field_3d engine with the SEAM K/L/M/N energy layer — the first concept to exercise energy_layer.h_ref_m as a genuine authored CHOICE that moves between two states showing the identical climb (STATE_1 vs STATE_3), and to pair two latched two-clause checkpoint stamps on one instrument to make a subtraction visible on screen (STATE_5). One canonical apparatus — a cart on a ramp, a U bar, and a dashed h = 0 line — carries three independent invariances, one per contrast pair: same place gives the same U (STATE_2, a state-function round trip), a moved zero shifts every U but never ΔU (STATE_3, the PRIMARY aha), and a different slope to the same height gives the same U (STATE_4, path independence). STATE_5 closes the loop by deriving U = mgh from potential_energy_definition's own ΔU = −W_conservative relation, applied to gravity, with two latched endpoint stamps proving the subtraction directly.

real_world_anchor.primary: A loaded cart pushed up a loading ramp — the ramp beside every delivery door, every warehouse and every station platform. Universal apparatus: no country, brand, festival or currency, and it is EXACTLY what the simulation draws, so the spoken anchor and the picture on screen are one object (Rule 25). The stored energy is exactly mgΔh between the two heights, a steeper ramp to the same platform stores the same energy, and where you call the floor is genuinely a choice — the h = 0 aha lives in the student's own everyday experience.
real_world_anchor.secondary: Water pumped to a rooftop tank. The stored energy is set only by how high the tank sits above the pump — open a tap and the stored energy comes back on its own.

h_ref_m.name: height of the chosen h = 0 line above the ramp's surface origin (the reference is a CHOICE, not a fact about the body) — a LIVE teacher control on STATE_3 and STATE_6, not merely an authored constant

s.name: position along the track, measured from the surface origin
s.derived: the integrator's own live value on driven/launched states; the slider-held value at rest in the explore

d.name: displacement from the state's own initial_position_m

h.name: height above the authored h = 0 line

U.name: gravitational potential energy — SIGNED: negative wherever the cart sits below the chosen h = 0 line, which is the whole point of STATE_3

F.name: applied drive force, along the surface, aiding the climb (S1/S3/S4 only — exactly balances mg sin(theta) so a = 0)

v.name: constant climb speed on the driven states (S1/S3/S4)

v0.name: launch speed at the state's own start, signed (S2/S5 only; zero/absent elsewhere)

a.name: acceleration along the surface (0 on driven states; -g*sin(theta) after launch on S2/S5, frictionless)

W_gravity.name: running work done BY gravity since the state's own initial_position_m (S5 ledger only)

formulas.delta_U: m * g * (h_end - h_start)  -- documentation only; both h values already net out h_ref_m, so this is reference-independent by construction
formulas.F_drive_balance: m * g * sin(radians(theta_deg))  -- S1/S3/S4: F is authored equal to this so a = 0 identically
formulas.a_after_launch: -g * sin(radians(theta_deg))  -- S2/S5: frictionless coast after v0
formulas.return_time_ms: 2000 * v0 / (g * sin(radians(theta_deg)))  -- S2/S5 home-recross wall time
formulas.rise_m: (v0 * v0) / (2 * g * sin(radians(theta_deg)))  -- S2 peak displacement above the launch s0

constraints: U = mgh at every instant, measured from THIS state's own authored h_ref_m -- never from an assumed ground; h_ref_m is a choice, not a physical fact.
ΔU = mgΔh is invariant under any repositioning of h_ref_m between two states that show the same climb (S1 vs S3): every individual U value shifts, the difference between two heights never does.
U is a state function: two visits to the same s (hence the same h) stamp the identical U regardless of the path taken between the visits (S2's round trip; S4's steeper path to S1's own height).

W_gravity = -ΔU_grav for gravity acting alone on the tracked body, for ANY choice of h_ref_m (S5) -- this is the potential_energy_definition relation, specialised to gravity and used to derive U = mgh.

h may go NEGATIVE, and on STATE_3 it is negative for most of the climb by design (h_ref_m = 1.5 m sits level with point B). Any state whose h can go below its own h = 0 line MUST author energy_layer.signed = true, which draws U_grav on a signed track about a mid-height zero baseline — the same shape the work ledgers use. The unsigned stack still cannot render a negative U_grav, so an unsigned state must keep h >= 0 at every instant of every authored loop including the +50 ms folded frame, or it fires the console warning THE EYE's H4 assertion reads as a failure. Signed states here: STATE_3 (h in [-1.20, 0.00] m) and STATE_6 (h_ref is a live slider). Unsigned states: STATE_1, STATE_2, STATE_4, STATE_5.

g = 9.8 m/s^2, constant at Earth's surface -- this concept never varies g and never leaves the h << R_Earth regime (the -GMm/r form is a later chapter, named once in advanced-ring narration only, never a formula here).

aha_moment.statement: There is no true zero height — you choose it, and only ΔU is physical.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The identical climb re-runs with the h = 0 line moved to the start: every U value shifts, yet ΔU stamps the same 29.4 J.

scene_composition.text: a 3 kg cart is driven up a 30° ramp at a steady 0.8 m/s, starting 0.3 m above the dashed h = 0 line
the U bar climbs in step with height: point A stamps 14.7 J at 0.5 m, point B stamps 44.1 J at 1.5 m, and the formula gains a second line, ΔU = mgΔh = 29.4 J
the displacement arrow d grows live from the release point, reading 2.40 m at point B

tts_sentences.text_en: Pushing this cart up the ramp stores energy in it: the higher it gets, the more it stores.
The stored energy grows from 14.7 J at point A to 44.1 J at point B.
The gain equals mass times gravity times the height climbed.

STATE_2.title: Back at the same height, same U

scene_composition.text: the same 3 kg cart launches up the same ramp at 3.13 m/s from 1.4 m above the line, coasts to a peak, and falls back
a home flag stamps 41.2 J the instant the cart departs, and stamps the same 41.2 J again the instant it returns — the place sets the energy, not the trip
the highest-point marker reads h = 1.90 m at the peak, computed live from the launch speed and the slope

tts_sentences.text_en: A cart is launched up the slope, rises, slows, and falls back to where it started.
Its stored energy reads 41.2 J at launch.
It reads the same 41.2 J on return.
The place sets the energy, not the trip.

STATE_3.title: The zero line is your choice

scene_composition.text: the identical climb from S1 (m = 3 kg, same speed, same two points) with ONE change: the dashed h = 0 line now sits level with point B, and it SLIDES there from S1's position as the state opens
the signed U bar opens at −35.3 J, well below its zero baseline, and rises to exactly 0.0 J at point B; point A now stamps −29.4 J — every reading has moved and the ones below the line are negative
the formula's second line still reads ΔU = mgΔh = 29.4 J, unchanged from S1 — only the zero line moved

tts_sentences.text_en: The zero line is your choice. Slide it, and only the numbers slide with it.
Here it sits level with point B, so point B itself now reads 0 J.
Below the line the stored energy is negative. That is allowed.
Every reading changed, yet the gain, 29.4 J, is exactly the same.

misconception_watch.belief: The ground is THE zero — a body at the ground HAS no potential energy, and U is an absolute property of the body.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The identical climb re-runs with the zero line moved to the start height — the bar now opens EMPTY and every stamped U changes, yet ΔU stamps the same 29.4 J.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: U depends on where you put zero; only ΔU = mgΔh is physical.

STATE_4.title: A steeper ramp, the same U

scene_composition.text: the ramp is rotated to 48.6° — steeper than S1's 30° — and the same 3 kg cart climbs at the same 0.8 m/s from the same 0.30 m start to the same 1.5 m height, with the 30° ramp drawn dim beside it
the displacement arrow reads d = 1.60 m at the flag, against the ghost ramp's d = 2.40 m over the identical Δh = 1.20 m, and the stamp is the identical 44.1 J
the applied-force arrow is longer here — more force was needed for the steeper climb, though the stored energy did not change

tts_sentences.text_en: Two ramps reach the same platform: the pale one gentle, this one steep.
The steep ramp is a shorter trip: 1.60 m instead of 2.40 m.
It reaches the same height, and the stamp is again 44.1 J.

misconception_watch.belief: Pushing a load up a LONGER ramp stores more potential energy — you pushed for longer.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: A steeper ramp reaches the same 1.5 m with d = 1.60 m instead of 2.40 m, and the stamp is the identical 44.1 J.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Only the height gained sets ΔU — path length does not enter mgΔh.

STATE_5.title: ΔU equals minus the work by gravity

scene_composition.text: S2's exact launch (3 kg, 3.13 m/s) with a second bar added: gravity's signed work ledger
a start flag latches U = 41.2 J and W gravity = 0.0 J the instant the cart departs; point C latches U = 51.5 J and W gravity = −10.3 J further up the slope
the formula surface reads ΔU = −W by gravity, with a second line ΔU = mgΔh = 10.3 J — the two stamped changes, 10.3 and −10.3, mirror exactly

tts_sentences.text_en: The cart starts 1.40 m above the line, reading 41.2 J.
It climbs to 1.75 m, and the reading rises to 51.5 J.
Neither starting number matters. Only the change does.
Gravity's work and the stored energy change equally and oppositely, 10.3 J each way.

scene_composition.text: a 2 kg cart rests on the ramp, held by friction, while the angle idles between 30° and 40° and the cart rides the turning ramp
drag the mass or angle sliders and the U bar re-derives live — U always equals mass times gravity times the height above the line
two live dials: mass m (1–3 kg) and incline angle θ (15°–40°)

tts_sentences.text_en: Drag the mass or the angle.
The ramp turns as the angle changes, and the cart rides with it.
U always equals mass times gravity times height.

regeneration_variants.label: A Suitcase Pulled Up an Airport Ramp
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A suitcase is pulled up a sloped luggage ramp toward the baggage-claim platform at a steady speed, past two marked points; the same ramp is later measured from the point where the suitcase starts.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical readings: the same U bar and the same two point-stamps, driven by the same U = mgh — moving the zero line moves every reading and never touches the gain between the two points.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same single-body rig, same inclined track — only the cart becomes a suitcase and the ramp becomes a luggage ramp.

regeneration_variants.label: A Crate Pushed Up a Loading-Dock Ramp
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A crate is pushed up a warehouse loading-dock ramp to a fixed platform height, once on a shallow ramp and once on a steep one.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same law, same numbers: the stamped potential energy at the platform height is identical on both ramps, even though the steeper ramp needs less travel distance to reach it.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same rig and physics — the cart is relabelled a crate, the ramp becomes a loading-dock ramp at two different slopes.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student who has mastered this concept can compute U = mgh for a body at a given height above a stated reference; explain that U's LEVEL shifts under a different chosen zero while ΔU between two positions never does; state that U is a state function depending only on height, never on speed or the path taken to reach it; predict that a steeper or shallower path to the same height gives the same U; and derive ΔU directly from the work done by gravity using ΔU = −W_gravity.

questions.stem: Compute U for a 2 kg bag placed on a shelf 3 m above the floor you are measuring from (g = 9.8 m/s²).

options.D: The answer cannot be found without knowing the true ground-level height

distractor_misconceptions.B: forgets to multiply by g, computing only m times h instead of mgh
distractor_misconceptions.C: borrows the one-half factor from kinetic energy's formula and halves mgh, which has no such factor
distractor_misconceptions.D: mistakes the chosen reference for an incomplete one — height measured above ANY chosen zero is enough; no absolute ground-level height is ever needed

questions.tested_idea: U = mgh from a height measured above a chosen reference — no 'true' zero is needed
questions.parallel_form_stem: Compute U for a 4 kg crate placed on a platform 1.5 m above the floor you are measuring from (g = 9.8 m/s²).

questions.stem: A cart is launched up a frictionless slope and returns to its exact starting height. Compare its potential energy U at departure and at return.

options.A: U is identical at departure and return — U depends only on height, and both instants are at the same height.
options.B: U at return is less, because the cart used energy fighting gravity on the way up.
options.C: U at return is greater, because gravity did positive work on the way down.
options.D: U cannot be compared without knowing the cart's speed at each instant.

distractor_misconceptions.B: invents a loss where none exists on a frictionless slope — nothing removes energy from U along the way; U is a pure function of position
distractor_misconceptions.C: assumes U changes because gravity did work on the most recent leg — U is set by height, not by which force acted most recently
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats U as dependent on speed — U is a pure function of position only, never of velocity

questions.tested_idea: U is a state function: the same position gives the same U, whatever path or speed brought the body there
questions.parallel_form_stem: A ball tossed straight up returns to the exact height it was thrown from. Compare its potential energy U at the moment it left the hand and the moment it returns to that height.

questions.stem: One student says a book's potential energy is 98 J; another says the same book, at the same position, has potential energy 40 J. Both are correct. How is this possible?

options.A: They measured height from two different chosen zero lines — U's level depends on the reference chosen, but ΔU between any two positions is the same for both.
options.B: One of them made an arithmetic mistake; only one value can be correct for the same book at the same position.
options.C: The book has two different masses in the two measurements.
options.D: Potential energy depends on which student is watching, so both values are simultaneously true.

distractor_misconceptions.B: the belief this state exists to correct — U's level genuinely changes with a chosen reference; no arithmetic error is required for two different, both-correct readings
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents a change in mass to explain a difference that is fully explained by a different height reference — nothing about the book itself changed
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats U as observer-dependent in an unphysical sense — the freedom is in the CHOSEN reference height, not in who is looking

questions.tested_idea: U's level shifts with the chosen zero reference; only ΔU is reference-independent
questions.parallel_form_stem: One student says a shelf's stored energy is 24.5 J; another says the same shelf, same book, same position, is 9.8 J. Both are right. How?

questions.stem: A crate is raised to the third floor once by a ramp and once by a straight vertical lift. Compare the change in potential energy ΔU for the two routes.

options.A: ΔU is identical for both routes — it depends only on the height gained, not on the path taken.
options.B: The ramp gives a smaller ΔU, because less force was needed to push it up.
options.C: The lift gives a smaller ΔU, because it took less time.
options.D: ΔU cannot be compared without knowing the exact shape of the ramp.

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses the FORCE needed with the ENERGY stored — a gentler ramp needs less force over a longer push, but the stored energy set by height is unchanged
distractor_misconceptions.C: invents a time-dependence for ΔU that does not exist — ΔU depends only on the height gained, not on how quickly it was gained
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats path independence as needing a path-specific correction — mgΔh contains no path-length or path-shape term at all

questions.tested_idea: ΔU depends only on the height gained, never on the path taken to gain it (path independence for gravity)
questions.parallel_form_stem: A trolley is raised to the same height once by a steep ramp and once by a gentle ramp. Compare ΔU for the two routes.

questions.stem: Gravity does −58.8 J of work lifting a crate from one point to another. State the change in the crate's potential energy ΔU between those two points.

options.C: U at the second point equals −58.8 J
options.D: ΔU cannot be found without knowing the reference height

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the minus sign in ΔU = −W by gravity — the change in U is the negative of the work gravity did
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses the CHANGE in U with the LEVEL of U at a point — the level needs a reference, the change does not
distractor_misconceptions.D: the relation ΔU = −W needs no reference height at all — only the LEVEL of U needs one, never the change

questions.tested_idea: ΔU = −W by gravity gives the change directly from the work done, independent of any chosen zero — the relation this state derives U = mgh from
questions.parallel_form_stem: Gravity does +19.6 J of work on a crate sliding down a ramp. State the change in the crate's potential energy ΔU.

questions.stem: A body's height above the chosen reference is fixed. Its mass is doubled. What happens to its potential energy U?

options.A: U doubles — U is directly proportional to mass at fixed height.
options.B: U stays the same — mass does not affect potential energy.
options.C: U quadruples — mass enters U the same way speed enters kinetic energy.
options.D: U cannot be found without knowing the body's speed.

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses potential energy with a quantity like acceleration under gravity, which genuinely is mass-independent — U = mgh has mass as a direct multiplying factor
distractor_misconceptions.C: borrows the squared dependence from kinetic energy's ½mv² — U depends on mass to the first power only
distractor_misconceptions.D: treats U as dependent on speed — U is a pure function of position (height) and mass only, never of velocity

questions.tested_idea: U is directly proportional to mass at fixed height — doubling m doubles U, no squared dependence
questions.parallel_form_stem: A crate's height above the floor is unchanged. Its mass is tripled. What happens to its potential energy U?

STATE_1.label: A 3 kg cart is driven up a frictionless 30° slope at a constant 0.8 m/s from s = 0.6 m (0.3 m above the h = 0 line); at s = 1.0 m point A stamps U = 14.7 J, at s = 3.0 m point B stamps U = 44.1 J, and at 4400 ms the formula gains a second line, ΔU = mgΔh = 29.4 J; the loop resets at 6000 ms.
STATE_1.caption: Higher up, more energy

STATE_2.label: The SAME 3 kg cart as S1 (Rule 32d: mass is pinned across S1–S5, only the taught variable changes) launches up the frictionless 30° slope at 3.13 m/s from s = 2.8 m (h = 1.4 m); a home-armed flag at s = 2.8 carries TWO stacked checkpoints, named by role so each caption stays true on every pass — 'first visit' latches 'U = 41.2 J' permanently at departure, 'this visit' re-stamps 'U = 41.2 J' on the return crossing (appearing as 'this visit (pass 2)' on the formula surface) and dwells there for 1400 ms — so departure and return are BOTH visible together on the formula surface during the return dwell; the predicted-stop marker reads 'highest point h = 1.90 m' at the peak (mass-independent: v₀²/2g sin θ), and the peak U = 55.9 J stays under bar_max_J = 60; the loop resets at 3178 ms.
STATE_2.caption: Same height, same energy

STATE_3.label: The identical S1 climb (m = 3 kg, v = 0.8 m/s, same s = 1.0 / 3.0 points) with energy_layer.h_ref_m moved to 1.5 m — LEVEL WITH POINT B, so the zero line's move is metres on screen rather than the old 0.3 m that was a few pixels (founder review 2026-08-10: 'state one, state three looks same'). Requires energy_layer.signed: true — U_grav goes negative here BY DESIGN, which is the concept's own misconception_watch and its negative_potential_energy drill-down. The signed U bar opens at −35.3 J, point A stamps U = −29.4 J, point B stamps U = 0.0 J; at 4400 ms the formula gains the same second line as S1, ΔU = mgΔh = 29.4 J; the loop resets at 6000 ms.
STATE_3.caption: New zero, same ΔU

STATE_4.label: The ramp is rotated to 48.6°; the same 3 kg cart drives up at 0.8 m/s from s = 0.4 m. s0 is 0.4, NOT S1's 0.6, deliberately: 0.4·sin 48.6° = 0.30 m, the SAME start height S1 uses, so both ramps climb the identical Δh = 1.20 m and the d comparison is one climb measured two ways rather than two different climbs (founder review 2026-08-10). At s = 2.0 m (the SAME h = 1.5 m as S1's point B) point B stamps U = 44.1 J with d = 1.60 m on the displacement arrow, against the 30° ghost_surface's d = 2.40 m drawn beside it at the same two heights; the loop resets at 3650 ms.
STATE_4.caption: Shorter path, same U

STATE_5.label: S2's exact launch (m = 3 kg — pinned across S1–S5, s0 = 2.8, v0 = 3.13 m/s) with a gravity work ledger added. A home-armed flag latches 'start (h = 1.40 m): U = 41.2 J · W gravity = 0.0 J' at departure; point C at s = 3.5 m latches 'point C (h = 1.75 m): U = 51.5 J · W gravity = −10.3 J', dwelling 1400 ms; the formula gains a second line, ΔU = mgΔh = 10.3 J, at 600 ms; the loop resets at 2900 ms. |W| = 10.3 J stays well inside work_scale_J = 30 and the peak U = 55.9 J inside bar_max_J = 60.
STATE_5.caption: Equal change, opposite sign

STATE_6.label: Sandbox: a 3 kg cart (the SAME mass S1–S5 use, so the teacher arrives at a recognizable home pose — Rule 32d) rides the ramp, held by static friction (μs = 0.9, μk = 0.8) at every authored angle. The idle sweep drives the cart's POSITION s between 1.2 m and 3.0 m, never θ: sweeping θ moved the very slider handle the caption tells the teacher to drag (founder review 2026-08-10), and s is the honest motion for U = mgh anyway — the cart climbs and the bar climbs with it. Three live controls: m, θ and the zero line h_ref, which is why this state needs energy_layer.signed (h_ref above the cart sends U negative). At the sweep and slider extremes U spans about −49.7 J to +56.7 J, inside the signed ±60 J track. U = mgh stands as the formula surface throughout; the sweep is cancelled for good by the first trusted drag (Rule 37).
STATE_6.caption: Change mass and angle yourself
